instruction: Add a header to the document containing the title text

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires adding a header to the document that contains the title text ('Libre Office: Open Source Word Processing' or similar). The evaluator checks if a header exists (50% score) and if it contains any of the key title words (50% score). Custom getter extracts header content from the first section, custom metric verifies presence and keyword matching.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts header content from the document's first section using python-docx library
Metric correctly handles 'expected' parameter for type='rule' (receives rules dict directly)
Postconfig appropriately saves document with Ctrl+S before verification to ensure changes are persisted
Keyword matching logic is too lenient - uses 'any()' to require only ONE keyword out of ['Libre', 'Office', 'Word', 'Processing']
Could award full score even if header contains just 'Word' or 'Office' without other meaningful title components
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider requiring multiple keywords (e.g., at least 2-3 out of 4) for full keyword score instead of just any single keyword
Alternative: Implement stricter matching that checks for meaningful combinations like 'Libre Office' or 'Word Processing'
Consider proportional scoring: award keyword score based on percentage of keywords found (e.g., 0.5 * (num_found / total_keywords))
